youtube.title: Rust Day 3: Cargo in 60 Seconds (new, run, check) 🦀
youtube.description:
Rust Day 3: Cargo, Rust's build tool and package manager, in 60 seconds. Create, build, run and check a project.

📌 In this short:
✅ cargo new creates a project: Cargo.toml + src/main.rs (+ a Git repo)
✅ cargo run builds and runs in one step; binaries go to target/debug
✅ cargo check is a fast "does it compile?"; cargo build --release optimizes

💻 Commands from the video:
cargo new hello_cargo
cd hello_cargo
cargo run
cargo check
cargo build --release

📖 Learn more: https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch01-03-hello-cargo.html
⏭️ Tomorrow: Variables & mutability

Follow for a new Rust lesson every day at 10 AM IST, from zero to pro 🦀
💬 Questions? Drop them in the comments 👇

scenes.say: Rust, day three. Meet Cargo, the tool almost every Rust project uses.

scenes.heading: Create a project
scenes.say: Cargo is Rust's build system and package manager, and it comes with rustup. Run cargo new hello underscore cargo. It creates a project folder, and even sets up a Git repository for you.
scenes.captions: Cargo is Rust's build system and package manager, and it comes with rustup. Run cargo new hello_cargo. It creates a project folder, and even sets up a Git repository for you.

scenes.heading: What Cargo made
scenes.caption: your code lives in src/
scenes.say: Cargo dot toml holds the project's name, version, edition, and dependencies. Your code lives in src, and main dot R S already has hello world in it.
scenes.captions: Cargo.toml holds the project's name, version, edition, and dependencies. Your code lives in src, and main.rs already has hello world in it.

scenes.heading: Build + run
scenes.say: Now cargo run. It compiles your code into the target slash debug folder, then runs it. Hello, world! One command instead of two.
scenes.captions: Now cargo run. It compiles your code into the target/debug folder, then runs it. Hello, world! One command instead of two.

scenes.heading: Three commands
scenes.say: cargo build only builds. cargo check just checks that your code compiles, without making a program, so it's much faster while you write code. And cargo build dash dash release makes an optimized build in target slash release.
scenes.captions: cargo build only builds. cargo check just checks that your code compiles, without making a program, so it's much faster while you write code. And cargo build --release makes an optimized build in target/release.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.say: Recap: cargo new starts a project, cargo run builds and runs, cargo check is a fast check, and dash dash release gives you an optimized build.
scenes.captions: Recap: cargo new starts a project, cargo run builds and runs, cargo check is a fast check, and --release gives you an optimized build.
